text: Just after midnight, outside a Mangwon convenience store, Jaeha sits over three cups of ramen while Nib eats kimbap without taking off his mask.
Then a pair of black boots, and a chair dragged right up against his.
A woman drops into it, far too close and perfectly at ease, with two canned coffees. He looks like he needs one, hero.
Jaeha goes red and looks anywhere but at her. That's very kind, miss, but they haven't met. Nib stares, unimpressed.
They have. Han Sora, twenty-seven, Black Hound's crossbow. She was behind Mok at Gate 0912.
The blush is gone. She was right behind Mok when that door closed.
She brings the briefing. Saturday, a B-grade gate in an old dam spillway, and Mok wants his hero to walk in first. For the cameras.
Of course, Jaeha smiles. He always walks in first.
His husks are famous now. Where did he find such strange ones? At a very strange shop, miss.
She leans closer. Do they eat, sleep, feel pain? Only ramen, only on the bus, and only when he forgets to feed them.
That gets a real laugh out of her.
On her wrist hangs a small brass compass. Its needle, a sliver of violet crystal, points vaguely between Jaeha and Nib.
Yesterday it pointed at him. But what is it really pointing at?
While she chats about bells in a drowned cathedral, Jaeha's hand slides under the table.
Through the link, he gives an order. Nib, field form, one second, then stop.
For one instant, Nib's eye flashes amber. Field form, cancelled after a second.
The needle swings hard at Nib.
Then the amber is gone, and the needle drifts back round until it only leans at Jaeha.
Sora glances at her wrist, surprised. Jaeha sips his coffee with a perfectly innocent face.
He notes it down. It snaps to summons in field form. When they rest, it only leans at him.
She stands with a knowing smile. See you Saturday, hero. Keep your husks close.
She walks off under the streetlamp, in no hurry at all.
Only then does Nib speak. She carries a piece of a boss on her wrist. Then when she's near, Jaeha says, they both stay in rest form.
Thursday morning on the rooftop, Borro has planted lettuce all along the rain gutter.
Seoa offers Nib one bag of shrimp crackers to fold the laundry. He wants two, and she has to taste them first.
Nib folds at lightning speed, perfectly serious, while Seoa proves the crackers are safe.
That afternoon, Bomi is serious for once. She's dug through every public raid record Black Hound has.
One stands out. The Han River gate, four years ago. One casualty: Oh Minseok, trap-tester. Cause: accident.
Jaeha goes very still.
Did he know him, Yerin asks. Minseok taught him everything in that notebook, and Jaeha was there when he died.
Choi arrives with kimbap and, for once, no smile. Bomi called him, so he pulled the incident report from the archive.
A yellowed page, a stamp, and a heavy signature.
Accident, signed by the officer in charge that night: Mok Hangyu.
Bomi and Yerin gasp. Jaeha doesn't move at all.
And there's one more name on it, Choi says quietly: the rescue responder that night. His own. He pulled a kid off that door, screaming that someone was still inside.
That kid was Jaeha.
And the colour drains out of the world.
Four years ago, in the Han River gate, an iron door grinds shut by itself, and two trap-testers run for the gap.
Minseok shoves young Jaeha through, and stays inside.
Through the last of the gap, he grins. Everyone comes back, kid. Go.
The door slams. Jaeha hammers on the iron with both fists.
A younger Choi drags him away, the boy still screaming that someone is in there.
Above the door, a small lamp is burning red.
Back on the rooftop, Jaeha and Choi just look at each other.
The lamp was red, Choi says. He wrote it down, and somebody took it out. Then they'll put it back.
Bomi is fierce. The whole country will be watching on Saturday, and whatever Mok does, she'll film it.
That night, Jaeha sits alone under a bare bulb while Borro sleeps with Nib curled in the hollow of his shell.
He turns to the oldest pages. The first twenty are in Minseok's handwriting. He could never throw them out.
In one margin, a stick figure in a vest gives a thumbs-up.
On a clean page, he writes three words. Mok. Minseok. Han River.
His eyes are wet, and hard.
The notebook snaps shut.
At the parapet, he looks out toward the river. Minseok said everyone comes back. He didn't.
In Borro's shell, one yellow eye opens.
Nib comes to stand beside him. The man who taught him went first for him. He did. And somebody closed the door on him.
Then on Saturday, says Nib, they open it.
Far off across the roofs, under one pier of a bridge, a faint white-cyan glow.
His phone buzzes. Unknown number. Sweet dreams, hero. Saturday, nine AM. Walk in first. Signed with a heart and an S.
Jaeha smiles, cold. He always does, Miss Han. That's the point.
